events.summary: English lead: "however soon turning into more of a Fascist movement".
English dates the ban to 21 November 1932. Finnish says the movement was banned in May 1932: dissolved on 24 March and confirmed by the court on 28 May.
English lead drops its fascist wording.
Finnish says the 1930 Peasant March was modelled on the 1922 March on Rome. The English account of the march leaves this out.
Finnish has a section on the historians’ debate over whether the movement was fascist. English states the label but has no passage on the debate.
Finnish traces the movement to the strike-breaking organisations of the late 1920s and the employers who funded them. English starts from the Comintern congress instead.
Finnish describes the movement’s colours, emblem and black shirt with blue stripes, partly modelled on the Italian Blackshirts. English has no text on its symbols.
The editions place the contested label differently: English puts "fascist" in its first sentence; Finnish discusses it in the last paragraph of its lead and in a section on the historians’ debate.

English calls the movement pro-Nazi in its first sentence (it said pro-German until April 2026). Finnish does not call the movement pro-Nazi. It reports a claimed secret agreement with the NSDAP as unreliable.

sql.label: Coverage on each 1 January
sql.query:
-- Coverage on one 1 January; run once per year, 2005-2026
SET @t = TIMESTAMP '2015-01-01 00:00:00';
SELECT AVG(nearest < 0.35) AS coverage, COUNT(*) AS passages
FROM (
  SELECT r.chunk_id, MIN(VEC_DISTANCE_COSINE(r.embedding, l.embedding)) AS nearest
  FROM chunk FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF @t AS r
  JOIN chunk FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF @t AS l
    ON l.wikidata_id = r.wikidata_id AND l.lang = 'en'
  WHERE r.wikidata_id = 'Q1412941' AND r.lang = 'fi'
  GROUP BY r.chunk_id
) AS m;

sql.label: Finding history
sql.query:
-- When each finding opened, was reviewed and closed:
-- every version of every row of the system-versioned finding table
SELECT id, type, status, summary, row_start, row_end
FROM finding FOR SYSTEM_TIME ALL
WHERE wikidata_id = 'Q1412941' AND lang = 'en'
ORDER BY row_start;
